name: Chairside Atlas
description: A 30-episode grand tour of everything an optometrist encounters from the moment a patient sits down to the final prescription — exam workflow, history, acuity, pupils, motility, slit lamp, fundus, refraction, and prescribing.

episodes.title: The First Sixty Seconds: Building Rapport and Reading the Patient
episodes.description: How the opening moments of an eye exam shape cooperation, trust, and the quality of history you can extract.

episodes.title: Chief Complaint and HPI: The Anchor of Every Exam
episodes.description: Structuring the history of present illness so it drives differential diagnosis rather than padding the chart.

episodes.title: Past Ocular History: What Old Records Reveal
episodes.description: Mining prior exams, surgeries, and medications for clues that change today’s plan.

episodes.title: Medical and Family History Through the Ocular Lens
episodes.description: Translating systemic disease into ocular risk — diabetes, hypertension, autoimmune, and hereditary patterns.

episodes.title: Medication Reconciliation: Ocular Side Effects You Cannot Miss
episodes.description: Building a mental library of drugs that threaten the retina, optic nerve, and surface.

episodes.title: Visual Acuity: More Than a Snellen Letter
episodes.description: Distance, near, contrast, and low-vision acuity — choosing the right chart and interpreting the number.

episodes.title: Pinhole Acuity: The Bedside Refractor
episodes.description: Using the pinhole to separate refractive from pathological vision loss in under a minute.

episodes.title: Near Vision and Presbyopia: Reading the Add
episodes.description: Assessing near demands, determining the add, and counseling patients on progressive versus single vision.

episodes.title: Color Vision Testing: Detecting Acquired Deficits
episodes.description: Ishihara, D-15, and Hardy-Rand-Rittler — congenital versus acquired color loss and what it signals.

episodes.title: Contrast Sensitivity: The Hidden Dimension of Sight
episodes.description: Pelli-Robson and beyond — why 20/20 patients still struggle to see at dusk or in glare.

episodes.title: Pupil Examination: The Direct and Consensual Pathway
episodes.description: A reproducible six-step pupil exam and what anisocoria at different light levels means.

episodes.title: The Swinging Flashlight Test: Catching a Relative Afferent Defect
episodes.description: Mastering the technique and interpretation of the RAPD — the single most useful bedside neuro-ophthalmic sign.

episodes.title: Confrontation Visual Fields: A One-Minute Screen
episodes.description: Four-quadrant and target-counting methods that catch hemianopias and quadrantanopias before formal perimetry.

episodes.title: Extraocular Motility: The Six Muscles and Their Nerves
episodes.description: Ductions, versions, cover-uncover in cardinal positions — and localizing a palsy in seconds.

episodes.title: The Cover Test and Cover-Uncover: Quantifying Ocular Deviation
episodes.description: Distinguishing tropia from phoria, measuring the shift, and knowing when to refer.

episodes.title: Slit Lamp Illumination: The Six Techniques and When Each Shines
episodes.description: Diffuse, direct focal, slit, retro, specular, and sclerotic scatter — matching technique to pathology.

episodes.title: Lids, Lashes, and Lacrimal Apparatus: The Anterior Survey
episodes.description: A systematic lid exam that catches blepharitis, entropion, lagophthalmos, and nasolacrimal obstruction.

episodes.title: Tear Film and Ocular Surface Assessment
episodes.description: TBUT, Schirmer, staining patterns, and meibography — a surface workup in under five minutes.

episodes.title: Conjunctiva: Reading Redness, Follicles, and Papillae
episodes.description: Differentiating infectious, allergic, and inflammatory conjunctivitis from the slit lamp pattern alone.

episodes.title: Cornea: Epithelium, Stroma, and Endothelium Layer by Layer
episodes.description: A repeatable corneal scan and the lesions that hide in each layer — abrasions, infiltrates, guttae.

episodes.title: Anterior Chamber: Depth, Cells, and Flare
episodes.description: Van Herick grading, cell/flare estimation, and recognizing the shallow chamber that changes everything.

episodes.title: Iris and Lens: Pupillary Margin to Nucleus
episodes.description: Iris transillumination, pseudoexfoliation, nuclear opalescence, and cortical spokes — a systematic lens exam.

episodes.title: Tonometry: Goldmann, iCare, and the Rebound Revolution
episodes.description: Technique, calibration, and when to trust — or doubt — a single IOP reading.

episodes.title: Gonioscopy: Opening the Angle
episodes.description: Indentation versus non-indentation, the Schaffer grading, and deciding who is a closure risk.

episodes.title: Fundus Examination Without Dilation: What You Can and Cannot See
episodes.description: Direct ophthalmoscopy, the 20D lens at the slit lamp, and the limits of the undilated view.

episodes.title: Dilated Fundus Examination: Disc, Macula, Vessels, Periphery
episodes.description: A four-zone retinal sweep that no pathology escapes — the 90D and 20D together.

episodes.title: Cup-to-Disc Ratio: Estimating and Documenting Accurately
episodes.description: Vertical and horizontal cupping, ISNT rule, and how to avoid the common estimation errors.

episodes.title: Macula and Foveal Reflex: Spotting Early Disease
episodes.description: Identifying drusen, pigmentary change, fluid, and the subtle foveal reflex loss that flags trouble.

episodes.title: Refraction: Retinoscopy to Subjective in Under Ten Minutes
episodes.description: A reproducible refraction flow from streak retinoscopy to Jackson cross cylinder and binocular balance.

episodes.title: Closing the Visit: Prescribing, Counseling, and Follow-Up
episodes.description: Translating the entire exam into a prescription, a plain-language plan, and the right recall interval.
